title: The Waif
scope: The accident, the crossings and their outcomes
premise: A car crash kills Ben's son. Ben finds a revolver, and every time he uses it on himself he wakes somewhere the crash went differently. What is actually happening to him?
ending: Ben ends up in a world where his family is alive, having never once undone the crash. Each shot left a world behind in which he died, and the worlds he woke into were already under way without him.

people.name: Ben
people.introduction: The man the film follows. He remembers nothing of the worlds he leaves.

people.name: The Waif
people.introduction: The woman who falls onto the car. She is the one person who remembers between worlds.

events.title: The falling-car accident splits the outcomes
events.text: A woman falls from an office window onto the roof of the family car. The crash separates into distinct outcomes, and the film follows only one of them.

events.title: The fall kills the Waif and Jack
events.text: In the outcome the film follows, the woman dies on the roof of the car and Jack is killed beside his father.

events.title: Jack lives; Ben dies in the accident
events.text: A separate outcome of the same crash, running from this moment onward. Jack survives it. The Ben of that outcome does not.

events.title: The Waif survives the fall
events.text: Another outcome of the same crash, running from this moment onward. The woman is not killed by the fall, and lives on in it.

events.title: The motel, the courthouse and the cabin
events.text: Ben's life after the crash. At the cabin he finds a book about how all of this works, and a revolver hidden in the crawlspace.

events.title: Ben pulls the trigger for the first time
events.text: Ben turns the revolver on himself. The moment separates: in one outcome the shot kills him, and the man we follow carries on elsewhere.

events.title: He dies at the shot in the storm
events.text: The outcome where the shot is simply fatal. This is where that perspective ends.

events.title: Ben wakes in the world where she lived
events.text: He comes round in the outcome where the woman survived the fall. It has been running without him, and the woman here is not the one who died on his car.

events.title: The living Waif arrives at the cabin
events.text: She comes to the door. She knows him, and she remembers what he does not.

events.title: He pulls the trigger again, at her encouragement
events.text: She tells him to do it. The moment separates again: one outcome keeps his body, the other keeps him.

events.title: He dies at the shot in the cabin
events.text: The outcome where this shot is fatal. That perspective ends here.

events.title: Ben wakes where Jack lived and he did not
events.text: He comes round in the outcome that separated at the crash, the one where Jack survived. It has been running since scene 10, and its own Ben died in the accident.

events.title: Jack is alive here, but this family watched Ben die
events.text: He has his son back and is a stranger in his own house. Later the house is attacked and Marie and Jack are killed.

events.title: He goes back to the cabin and fires again
events.text: After the reunion fails he returns to the cabin and uses the revolver a third time.

events.title: He dies at the last shot
events.text: The outcome where the last shot is fatal. That perspective ends here.

events.title: The light stays red and Jack draws on the glass
events.text: A morning that resembles the opening: the family are together in the car and the boy draws on the window. Nothing connects this to what happened to Ben.

chapters.title: The crash and what it separates
chapters.introduction: The accident does not have one result. Follow the outcome the film follows, and keep the other two in mind: they carry on without being shown.

chapters.title: The first crossing
chapters.introduction: The revolver does not undo the crash. It separates the moment, and the man we follow wakes somewhere that was already happening.

chapters.title: The second crossing
chapters.introduction: The second shot puts him in the outcome that separated back at the crash, where his son survived and he did not.

chapters.title: The last shot, and the morning after
chapters.introduction: A third shot, a third outcome left behind, and a closing morning that belongs to no part of his journey.

sources.title: Repository story record
sources.note: Editorial pilot adapted from the repository encoding. Scene wording and interpretation await review against the primary work.

flowchart.title: The accident, the crossings and their outcomes
flowchart.description: The crash separates into three outcomes. Ben crosses into two of them; each crossing leaves behind an outcome in which he died.
flowchart.frame: Read downwards. An outcome begins at the moment that separates it, and keeps running afterwards whether or not the film shows it. Arrows that move a person are dashed; they never create the place they arrive at.
